results.title: Containerization – your path to modern software development
results.content: # Containerization – your path to modern software development. Containers are lightweight, start up quickly, and provide a consistent environment across different stages of the application lifecycle – from development to testing and production. 1. **Microservices architecture** – Businesses transitioning to a microservices architecture can use containers for packaging, deploying, and managing each service independently. 2. **Multi-cloud deployments** – Containerization supports multi-cloud strategies by ensuring that applications run consistently across different cloud environments. 3. **Scalable cloud-native apps** – Containerization is ideal for applications that need to be scaled up and down quickly. 6. **Isolated development environments** – Containers provide senior software engineers with isolated development environments that match the production environment. 7. **Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) products** – Containerization is highly beneficial in developing and deploying SaaS products. 8. **Machine learning** – Containers manage the complexities of machine learning applications, which often have numerous dependencies. Wrapping a machine learning model and its dependencies into a container can make it easier to move the model between different stages of the ML lifecycle – from development to testing and production. * **App portability** – Containers can run on any system supporting containerization technology. * **Consistency and reproducibility** – Since the application and its dependencies are packaged together, containers ensure consistency across different environments. * **App isolation** – Each container runs in isolation, ensuring that the application has all the resources it needs and won’t interfere with other containers. * **Simplified dependency management** – Containers bundle the application code along with its dependencies. * **Fast deployment and start-up time** – Containers can be started in seconds, which is significantly faster than virtual machines. These tools help manage containers at scale – handling tasks like deployment, networking, scaling, and load balancing. 1. **Container platforms** – Docker sits at the forefront, providing tools to package applications into containers that contain the application and all its dependencies. 3. **Develop a containerization strategy** – Your strategy should include details on the architecture (such as microservices or monolithic), the container platform, the orchestration tool, and the cloud provider, if applicable. You need senior software engineers who know containerization and agile product managers who already think in containers and microservices.

results.title: Docker Ensuring Consistency and Reproducibility in Software Environments | by Viheet jalmi | Medium
results.content: # Docker Ensuring Consistency and Reproducibility in Software Environments. The development team is facing challenges in ensuring consistent and reproducible environments for software development, testing, and deployment across different machines and platforms. The lack of environment standardization leads to inconsistencies, dependency conflicts, and compatibility issues, causing delays in development cycles and hindering collaboration among team members. Docker can provide a solution to the problem by enabling consistent and reproducible environments through containerization. 1. Environment Standardization: Docker allows developers to package their applications, along with their dependencies and configurations, into lightweight and portable containers. By using Docker, development teams can ensure that the application runs consistently across different machines and environments, eliminating compatibility issues and reducing configuration-related errors. 2. Dependency Management: Docker allows for precise control over the dependencies required by the application. Docker also provides mechanisms to easily update or roll back dependencies, simplifying the management of complex software stacks. 3. Reproducible Builds: With Docker, the build process becomes reproducible. Docker images are built from Dockerfiles, which contain step-by-step instructions to create the environment. By sharing the Dockerfile with the team, anyone can reproduce the exact same environment by building the Docker image. This eliminates the “it works on my machine” problem and allows for consistent builds and testing across different development machines and deployment environments. 4. Collaboration and Continuous Integration: Docker facilitates collaboration among team members by providing a consistent environment for development, testing, and deployment. Developers can share Docker images or Dockerfiles, allowing others to quickly spin up the same environment on their machines. Applications packaged in Docker containers can be easily scaled horizontally by running multiple instances of the same container across different hosts or cloud environments. Docker’s orchestration tools, such as Docker Swarm or Kubernetes, facilitate the management and scaling of containerized applications, ensuring high availability and efficient resource utilization. By leveraging Docker’s containerization technology, development teams can solve the problem of inconsistent and reproducible environments. Docker enables standardization, simplifies dependency management, ensures reproducible builds, promotes collaboration, and facilitates scalable production deployments. Adopting Docker as part of the development and deployment workflow can lead to improved productivity, reduced errors, and faster software delivery.

results.title: Containerization and R for Reproducibility and More – R Consortium
results.content: # Containerization and R for Reproducibility and More. ## Abstract. Containerization has become a dominant computing paradigm for computing in the past decade due to its many advantages: isolation and security, scalability and efficiency with lightweight containers sharing an operating kernel and resources, and portability across cloud computing providers. For the researcher, analyst, or R user, containers have applications ranging from reproducible analytical environments to packaging statistical code to use in web applications. I will discuss how biomedical researchers can make use of containerization technology, particularly the tools provided by the Rocker Project, which publishes powerful standardized containers for the R language. ## Speaker. Noam Ross is a computational disease ecologist and Executive Director of rOpenSci, a nonprofit dedicated to promoting open science and validating data science and computational methods. He is a core member of the Rocker Project, which maintains standardized containers for the R computer language. Noam’s work includes spearheading rOpenSci’s work in software peer review, developing a widely emulated system for leveraging the academic peer-review process coupled with state-of-the art automated code analysis to improve code quality in the scientific software in ecosystem, as well as using review as a mechanism for community building and training. His research interests and contributions span a wide range of topics, including disease ecology, zoonotic spillover, mechanistic modeling of disease dynamics, and non-parametric data science methods. His applied work includes creating early outbreak assessment models for the U.S. Defense Threat Reduction Agency, and modeling and forecasting for New York State’s COVID-19 emergency response. Noam holds a Ph.D. in theoretical ecology from the University of California-Davis and a B.Sc. from Brown University.

results.title: Reproducibility in Scientific Computing
results.content: Reproducibility is a cornerstone of scientific research, ensuring that results can be reliably verified and built upon. In the context of scientific computing, reproducibility refers to the ability to obtain consistent results using the same data, code, and computational environment. Reproducibility is defined as the ability to reproduce the results of a computational experiment using the same data, code, and computational environment^1. * **Better reuse**: Reproducible research enables the reuse of data and code, reducing the need for redundant computations. This section will discuss the use of version control systems like Git, documenting code and research workflows, and utilizing containerization tools like Docker. Documenting code and research workflows is essential for reproducibility. Containerization tools like Docker enable researchers to create reproducible computational environments. To ensure reproducibility, researchers should adhere to best practices, including organizing code and data, using open-source and transparent methods, and ensuring computational reproducibility. ### Organizing Code and Data for Reproducibility. Organizing code and data is crucial for reproducibility. * Use transparent and reproducible methods for data analysis and processing. * Use containerization tools like Docker to create reproducible computational environments. \[\text{Reproducibility} = \frac{\text{Same Data} + \text{Same Code} + \text{Same Computational Environment}}{\text{Same Results}}\]. By employing strategies like version control, documentation, and containerization, and adhering to best practices, researchers can ensure that their research is reproducible and contributes to the advancement of scientific knowledge. Reproducibility in scientific computing refers to the ability to obtain consistent results using the same data, code, and computational environment. ### Why is reproducibility important in scientific research? Reproducibility is essential in scientific research because it ensures that results are reliable and verifiable, facilitating collaboration and accelerating scientific progress. ### How can I achieve reproducibility in my research? To achieve reproducibility, you can employ strategies like version control, documentation, and containerization, and adhere to best practices like organizing code and data, using open-source and transparent methods, and ensuring computational reproducibility. Common challenges in achieving reproducibility include the complexity of computational environments, lack of documentation, limited availability of data and code, and evolving software and hardware. You can use tools like Git for version control, Docker for containerization, and Jupyter Notebooks for documenting and executing code to achieve reproducibility.

results.title: Where To Publish Your Code - Research Software: Designing for Publication and Reproducibility - Research Guides at New York University
results.content: # Research Software: Designing for Publication and Reproducibility. How to prepare scholarly code for submission to journals or repositories. We recommend publishing your code in an open-source repository that will do the following:. * Assign a DOI (digital object identifier), a persistent link to your software that's more permanent than a URL, so your software can be cited and remain accessible. Some journals may have their own requirements for how you publish and provide access to your software; for example, they may ask you to place your work in a repository that permits anonymous reviewer access. It's also possible that you will want to put data in one repository--perhaps because of its size, or because a certain data repository is standard within your discipline--while storing code elsewhere. ### I Put My Software on GitHub, Isn't That Enough? Also, developers in countries that face US sanctions or have governments that impose internet censorship may have limited access to GitHub. In many cases, GitHub (or GitLab, or BitBucket, or another similar site) may be where you and most of your users interact with the software. However, a stable copy can and should live in the longer term in a designated repository that can assign a DOI to your work. This GitHub Action allows a user to upload a GitHub repository (or a designated folder in a GH repository) directly to a Dataverse dataset. Users create a "dataverse" which can include data, code, and related papers; each is assigned a DOI and each has file-level metadata. OSF allows users to upload software as a zip file rather than displaying the entire repository, and does not provide for software versioning. However, if you have the rest of the project's data in OSF, your software can be stored there, as well. Zenodo is currently the best repository for storing research code. It can connect directly to a GitHub repository and use its API to pull in a copy of your software and its metadata. Zenodo assigns DOIs, and provides users with a badge they can place on the readme file of their repos includes the DOI and with it, the proper citation for the code.
